source_name: Microgramm – davčne blagajne / SimPos ECR with integrated POS terminal
source_subtype: POS/ECR vendor site with public pricing
why_relevant: SME-segment fiscal cash register vendor bundling an ECR with a connected payment terminal (S1F2) at a published monthly rental price (~EUR 22.7 + VAT). Published pricing and bundle composition are hard evidence of the economics of merchant acceptance at the long tail of Slovenian retail and hospitality.

source_name: Krajnik d.o.o. – professional POS hardware distributor (Sunmi, Sam4s, EloPOS, Jassway, Shuttle)
why_relevant: Distributor catalogue revealing which POS hardware brands actually reach the Slovenian market and at what price points — an indirect but reliable read on terminal/ECR hardware supply chains and refresh cycles in SI retail and hospitality.

source_name: POS Elektronček – Slovenian POS/ECR and remote-ordering vendor
why_relevant: Established SI checkout vendor (GIS Order Android remote-ordering system) serving hospitality and retail; part of the domestic vendor map that determines how easily an acquirer or terminal vendor can integrate at the till.

source_name: MetaKocka / Birokrat / Minimax / Vasco – cloud fiscal cash-register and ERP software vendors
why_relevant: Software layer of the Slovenian till: these vendors implement the FURS DPR interface and expose which accounting/POS ecosystems interoperate (Birokrat, Minimax, Pantheon, OpPIS, Vasco, Hermes). Their integration and export documentation maps the practical constraints on adding a card-acceptance flow to an SME merchant's checkout.

source_name: Worldline / SIX Payment Services Slovenia – merchant acceptance product pages
why_relevant: Acquirer/PSP-side view of the SI merchant market: which schemes and wallets are accepted, terminal families offered (incl. Tap on Mobile softPOS), and how acceptance is packaged for small merchants. Directly documents what merchants can buy for card acceptance in Slovenia.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. – POS terminal management and servicing; annual reports
source_subtype: card processor corporate site + annual report PDFs
why_relevant: The Slovenian processor that operates and services a large share of the national POS estate for member banks and accepts international and local schemes (Maestro, MC, Visa, Amex, Diners, BA, Karanta, Activa). Its annual reports and service pages are the closest public description of who physically runs Slovenian merchant terminals.

source_name: 'Slovenija plačuje digitalno' (Visa + banks + GZS) programme pages
why_relevant: A named, dated market intervention explicitly targeting the weak spot of SI merchant acceptance: micro/small merchants. Publishes eligibility rules (free/subsidised terminal for at least 9 months for merchants with no card acceptance in the past 12 months) and participating banks (OTP, NLB). It is both a demand-side stimulus to track and an implicit admission of the size of the non-accepting merchant base.

source_name: Slovenian business/consumer press reporting merchant-level cash-vs-card splits (24ur, Žurnal24, Forbes SI, Siol, Svet kapitala)
why_relevant: Only public channel where individual Slovenian merchants disclose till-level payment mix — e.g. Petrol reporting roughly 50% of purchases in cash and Mercator somewhat under 60% cash. These merchant-sourced figures exist nowhere in official statistics and are the richest merchant-side quantitative signal available.

source_name: Retail technology trade press on SI self-checkout deployments (Retail Technology, iXtenso, ESM Magazine)
why_relevant: Documents named self-checkout deployments in Slovenia by international vendors (e.g. NCR self-checkouts ordered for 12 SPAR INTERSPAR hypermarkets) and supplies chain-level share and store-count context (Mercator ~742 stores / 30.5%; Spar ~134 stores / 26.7% in 2022). Complements the domestic vendor view with the international-vendor view of the same estate.

source_name: Commercial market-research reports on the Slovenia POS terminal market (Mordor Intelligence, Statista)
why_relevant: Vendor-side sizing and forecast of the SI POS terminal market (CAGR figures, segment splits) and long time series of terminal counts. Useful as a triangulation layer and for competitor/vendor share hypotheses, but methodology is opaque and headline numbers should never be preferred over Banka Slovenije counts.

source_name: Stripe – Payments in Slovenia market guide
why_relevant: PSP-authored country guide summarising merchant-relevant acceptance facts (card share of POS transaction value and count, contactless penetration, preferred local methods). Convenient orientation layer for the merchant acceptance mix, though derived from third-party data and commercially framed.

source_name: HRC d.o.o. — Hibis core banking platform (Slovenian bank reference list)
why_relevant: Slovenian core-banking software house whose own site claims >50% of the Slovenian banking market runs Hibis and names its bank customers explicitly (NLB, OTP banka, Deželna banka Slovenije, Addiko, Gorenjska banka, BKS Bank, Delavska hranilnica, LON, Primorska hranilnica Vipava, RCI Banque). This is the single richest vendor-side map of who runs which core/digital-channel stack in SI, exposing go-live events (e.g. DBS fully on Hibis from 1.1.2025) that neither the banks nor Banka Slovenije publish.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf investor press releases — Bankart / Vynamic Transaction Middleware
why_relevant: Vendor press release (13 May 2024) discloses that Bankart, Slovenia's dominant card/payment processor, is replacing its legacy Base24 platform with Diebold Nixdorf Vynamic Transaction Middleware, serving ATMs, POS and e-commerce for ~20 banks in six SEE countries. Quantifies estate scope and switch-migration timing — exactly the procurement detail that is otherwise invisible.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. annual reports (letno poročilo) — vendor and ATM-fleet disclosures
why_relevant: Bankart's annual reports name the ATM makes in the managed fleet (NCR, Wincor Nixdorf, Diebold, Diebold Nixdorf) and describe processing volumes and platform projects. Because Bankart processes for most SI banks, this is the closest thing to an aggregate ATM/POS estate inventory, and it doubles as a vendor-mapping source.

source_name: Temenos success stories — Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB)
why_relevant: Vendor case study documenting Temenos core at NLB since 2002 (corporate first, then retail, incl. N Banka retail migration) with quantified claims (time-to-market -50%, onboarding +20% faster, multicurrency accounts). Establishes NLB's core-banking dependency and upgrade cadence, plus the N Banka integration timeline.

source_name: Nets (Nexi Group) / Bankart instant-payments infrastructure announcement (FinTech Futures coverage)
why_relevant: Documents that Nets deployed and operates the RealTime24/7 instant-payments solution behind Bankart's national SCT/SCT Inst infrastructure — i.e. the technology supplier under Slovenia's instant-payment (Flik) rails. Key for understanding who controls SI payment-statistics-generating infrastructure.

source_name: Printec Group — Slovenia self-service / ATM deployments (corporate site + social newsroom)
why_relevant: Regional B2C transaction-technology integrator and NCR SelfServ channel partner active in SI; its posts name concrete deployments (e.g. a post stating Printec installed the first NCR SelfServ 27 ATM in Slovenia for SKB). Vendor-side evidence of ATM refresh cycles and which bank buys which OEM.

source_name: Euronet Worldwide IR newsroom + Euronet Slovenija banks page (IAD / ATM-as-a-Service)
source_subtype: vendor bank-partner page + investor press releases
why_relevant: Euronet is an independent ATM deployer and outsourcer active in CEE incl. Slovenia; its bank-facing page markets ATM-as-a-Service, network participation agreements and asset-purchase programmes — the mechanism by which bank-owned ATM estates shrink and IAD estates grow. IR press releases date market entries and deposit-terminal (ADT) rollouts.

source_name: Halcom d.d. — multibank e-banking (Hal E-Bank) and supported-banks list
source_subtype: vendor site + support/knowledge base bank list
why_relevant: Slovenian payments/e-banking and digital-certificate vendor. Its own pages quantify usage (250k+ business users, ~13m payments/month, ~EUR 40bn monthly value) and its support pages enumerate which Slovenian banks are reachable through Hal E-Bank (Addiko, Banka Sparkasse, BKS Bank, Delavska hranilnica, Gorenjska banka, …). Rare vendor-published proxy for corporate payment volumes plus a bank-coverage map.

source_name: Kontron Slovenia (ex S&T Slovenija) — financial-industry / CORE banking solutions pages
why_relevant: Large SI systems integrator with a dedicated 'CORE bančne rešitve' / financial-services solutions line; integrator pages and case studies are a standard route to bank IT project disclosure (infrastructure, SAP, core banking, ATM/branch infrastructure).

source_name: ASEE / Asseco South Eastern Europe — Slovenia entity and banking offering
why_relevant: ASEE runs a registered Slovenian entity (Litostrojska cesta 44c, Ljubljana) and sells omnichannel/banking software across SEE; its group structure and services pages are the entry point to case studies naming regional bank clients. Confirms an in-country vendor presence competing for SI bank software work.

source_name: Payten (ASEE Group) — ATM/POS managed services and processing
why_relevant: Payten is the ASEE payments arm covering eCommerce, mPayments, processing and ATM/POS related services across 23 countries incl. the SI region — a direct competitor/supplier in the SI terminal estate. Its client and news pages are a route to POS/ATM deployment facts not published by banks.

source_name: Humanfrog — case study: Sberbank banka (Slovenia)
why_relevant: Small SI digital agency publishing a named bank case study (Sberbank banka, the SI entity later absorbed into NLB as N Banka). Illustrates the long tail of small vendors that name SI bank clients — useful for digital-channel and campaign-side intelligence and for reconstructing the Sberbank→N Banka→NLB transition.

source_name: Logate — case study: NLB Banka Podgorica (CX360)
why_relevant: Regional vendor case study on an NLB Group subsidiary. NLB Group standardises platforms across markets, so subsidiary-level vendor references are a leading indicator of what may be rolled into the Slovenian parent — a classic indirect route into an otherwise opaque group procurement.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — Slovenia/Bankart ATM and payments vendor coverage
why_relevant: Trade publication that reliably re-reports ATM/payments vendor announcements including SI ones; useful as a low-cost aggregator to catch vendor press releases whose originating newsrooms are hard to poll, and to snowball to further vendors and estate numbers.

source_name: Slovenian media coverage of bank IT platform migrations (BKS Bank platform switch fallout)
why_relevant: When a vendor/platform migration fails publicly, SI media describe the systems involved in detail (BKS Bank SI moved core banking and payments onto the Austrian parent's new platform; duplicate direct debits, wrong statements, Flik issues). Failure reporting is one of the few routes that dates and names bank platform changes in local language.

source_name: Comtrade programske rešitve d.o.o. (Ljubljana) — SI software house serving finance
why_relevant: Comtrade's Slovenian entity (Letališka cesta 29B, Ljubljana; ~310 staff, ~EUR 42m revenue 2024) is a significant local software supplier whose corporate registry footprint and bank-account relationships (NLB, OTP banka) confirm financial-sector exposure. Registry/credit portals are the pointer that lets you size otherwise-private vendors before hunting their reference pages.
